name: Airbus H145 / EC145 / UH-72 Lakota
summary: Light-medium twin used widely for US air ambulance and police work; the Army's UH-72 Lakota is the standard National Guard utility and flight-training helicopter.

wings: Four-blade main rotor (EC145/D2) or five-blade bearingless rotor (H145 D3)
engines: Two engines side by side on the roof with exhausts at the rear of the cowling
fuselage: Tall, boxy cabin with large sliding side doors
Rear clamshell doors under a high-mounted tail boom
Tall skids lifting the cabin well off the ground
Army versions in black or green with 'ARMY' titles
tail: EC145 / UH-72A: open two-blade tail rotor

tellTales: Tall, boxy twin-engine cabin perched on high skids
Clamshell doors under a high tail boom
Big sliding side doors on a light twin

confusedWith.howToTell: The H145 is larger and taller with high skids and sliding doors; the H135 is compact, low and always has a Fenestron.
The 429 has a rounder, lower cabin and a scissor four-blade tail rotor; the H145 has a tall box cabin with a two-blade or Fenestron tail.
The AW139 is larger with five blades, retractable wheels and sponsons; the H145 sits on skids.
The BK 117 is a smaller, boxier pod; the H145 is larger with a longer, sleeker cabin and a different nose.
The Bo 105 is a short stubby pod with a very short mast; the H145 is much larger with sliding doors.

usCount.source: US Army ~470 UH-72A/B (Army 2025) + ~270 FAA-registered EC145/H145 (BK117 C-2/D-2/D-3)
